verses.1: And Naaman, the king of Israel, was a great man in his time. His face was beautiful, as if it had been given to him by Jehovah as a sign of His favor toward Israel. This man was also a powerful warrior.
verses.2: And Aram’s people departed, leaving their land. There was a little girl who stood before Naamán’s wife.
verses.3: And she said to her servant, “May my Lord bless him before the prophet who is in Shomron. Then he will be rescued from his suffering.”
verses.4: And he came and reported to his master, “Thus and thus spoke the girl from the land of Israel.”
verses.5: And the king of Aram said, “Go and send a message to the king of Israel.” He went and took with him twelve silver coins, six thousand gold coins, and ten pieces of clothing.
verses.6: And the scribe came before the king of Israel and said, “Now, as this scroll is brought before you, I have sent my servant Naaman to you. He has been cured from his disease.”
verses.7: And when the king of Israel called for the book, he tore his clothes and said, “God, I will die and be resurrected. This is who has been sent to me to gather men from their sins. Please know that he is a liar.”
verses.8: And when Elisha heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent a message to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Come before me, so that I may know that there is indeed a prophet among the people of Israel.”
verses.9: And Naaman came in his chariot and horse, and he stood at the door of Elijah’s house.
verses.10: And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you will be clean and able to return.”
verses.11: And Naaman became angry. He went away and said, “Look! I have said to myself, ‘He will go and stand there, and call out in the name of the LORD God of Israel.’” Then he raised his hand towards that place, and the leprosy disappeared.
verses.12: It is not good to trust in them. They are like rotten branches from all the ages of Israel. I will not wash them clean; they remain unclean. They will go away in a hurry.
verses.13: And his servants came and spoke to him. They said, “My father, this is a great message from the prophet. He has told us not to do this. Even though he said to us, ‘Wash yourself and be pure.’”
verses.14: And he went down into the river, and bathed seven times, as commanded by God. Then he sat down on his back, just like a little boy.
verses.15: And he sat down before the Lord, along with all his followers. He stood before Him and said, “Now, I know that there is no God in all the world, except in Israel. Now, please take a blessing from your servant.”
verses.16: And He said, “The Lord who stands before me: if I take it, may he be destroyed.”
verses.17: And Naaman said, “Please do not allow me to serve you. I cannot serve you anymore. He will not worship other gods instead of Jehovah.”
verses.18: For this reason, Jehovah will forgive your servants when He comes to the house of Rimmon to worship. He will take me by the hand, and I will worship in the house of Rimmon. When I worship in the house of Rimmon, Jehovah will forgive your servants for this matter.
verses.19: And he said to him, “Go and comfort him.” So he went away from him, as if he were a wanderer in the wilderness.
verses.20: And Giehazi said, “Young man Elisha, man of God! Look here: I am about to take from him what he has brought from Jehovah’s life. As if I wanted to follow in his footsteps and take from him even more.”
verses.21: And Gehazi followed Naaman. When Naaman saw that Gehazi was running behind him, he fell off his donkey. Then Naaman said, “Be at peace.”
verses.22: And Shalom said to his servant, “Now, these two young men from Ephraim, who are among the prophets, please be given to them as gifts: a silver plate and two sets of clothes.”
verses.23: And Naaman said, “Take some gold coins.” He then broke them into pieces. He made two golden rings and two bracelets from those pieces of gold. He gave them to his two sons, and they carried them before him.
verses.24: And he went to the tent, took something from it, burned it in the house, and then sent those people away. They left.
verses.25: And he came and stood before his Lord. He said to Him, “Elisha, I am your servant. Do not leave me.”
verses.26: And he said to him, “My heart did not go with him when he got off his chariot to come and call for you at the appointed time. He came to take the money, along with clothes, olives, grapes, sheep, cattle, servants, and women.”
verses.27: And the curse of Naamán will be upon you and your descendants forever. And from before him will come a curse like snow.
